chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ayyam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The beginning of Al-Aqiq is Barid Al-Baath, and it is six miles from Al-Maslakh on the side facing Iraq, and between it and Ghumrah are twenty-one miles, two Barids.

key_terms.الْعَقِيقِ: A valley and place near Mecca, a boundary for prayer and rituals
key_terms.الْعِرَاقَ: Iraq, indicating the direction from Mecca
key_terms.الْمَسْلَخِ: The place of slaughter, referring to the Masjid Al-Haram/Kaaba area
key_terms.بَرِيدُ الْبَعْثِ: A specific station or location named Barid Al-Baath

ai.seo_question: What is the location and distance of Al-Aqiq from the Kaaba?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* precisely delineates the starting point of Al-Aqiq, a key miqat (ritual boundary) for pilgrims entering the state of Ihram, situated six miles from the Miqat of Al-Maslakh towards Iraq. By anchoring the boundary in specific historical landmarks like Barid Al-Baath and Ghumrah, it reflects the scholarly tradition of reconciling geographical measurements with ritual obligations to ensure the validity of Hajj and Umrah.
